options.title: Review bed allocation process
options.description: The policy expects CTAS 1 or CTAS 2 patients to have immediate access to a monitored bed on arrival. Records suggest that this may not always be the case, possibly due to high bed occupancy or a slow physician pace. Reviewing the bed allocation process could identify any gaps or inefficiencies that may be contributing to this issue.
options.local_fit: This option aligns with the observed conditions of high bed occupancy and a slow physician pace, which may be contributing to the lack of immediate access to monitored beds for CTAS 2 patients. Reviewing the bed allocation process could help identify any local factors or bottlenecks that may be unique to this context.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If the bed allocation process is adjusted, pressure may shift to the roles responsible for implementing the new process, such as the Charge Nurse and Physician Lead. It is important to ensure that any changes are communicated and supported effectively to minimize disruption.
options.how_we_would_know: Reviewing the bed allocation process and any related documentation or guidelines would provide insights into the current practices and potential areas for improvement. Engaging with the relevant roles and seeking their feedback would also help validate the findings and ensure a comprehensive understanding of the issue.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the review identifies no significant issues or improvements in the bed allocation process, or if the observed conditions of high bed occupancy and slow physician pace resolve, the review may be discontinued.

options.title: Monitor and escalate wait times
options.description: The policy expects CTAS 1 or CTAS 2 patients to have immediate access to a monitored bed on arrival. However, records suggest that this may not always be the case. Monitoring and escalating wait times could help identify any delays or bottlenecks in the system.
options.local_fit: This option aligns with the observed condition of a slow physician pace, which may be contributing to delays in accessing monitored beds. By monitoring and escalating wait times, the team can gain insights into the impact of physician pace on patient flow and take appropriate action.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If wait times are consistently above thresholds, pressure may shift to the Physician Lead to address the slow pace and create capacity. It is important to ensure that the Physician Lead has the necessary support and resources to address the issue effectively.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitoring wait times and tracking the frequency and duration of delays would provide quantitative data to assess the impact of physician pace on patient flow. Engaging with the Physician Lead and understanding their perspective on the issue would also be valuable in developing targeted solutions.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If monitoring reveals that wait times consistently meet the expected standards, or if the observed condition of a slow physician pace resolves, the monitoring may be discontinued.

recommendation.rationale: Given the observed condition of a slow physician pace, monitoring wait times is a targeted approach to addressing the issue.
recommendation.would_change_if: If the observed condition of a slow physician pace is not confirmed, or if there are significant changes in the bed allocation process, the recommendation may shift.

suggested_reviewers.why: The Bed Management Team Lead can provide insights into the bed allocation process and potential improvements.
The Physician Lead can offer perspectives on the slow physician pace and its impact on patient flow.

options.title: Escalation huddles
options.description: Trigger escalation huddles when wait-time thresholds are exceeded, particularly during periods of high bed occupancy and slow physician pace.
options.local_fit: This option aligns with existing practices and could be implemented quickly. However, it may not address the root cause of the issue, which is the slow physician pace.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to nurses and patients if physicians are unable to keep up with the pace of rooming during huddles. Additionally, the burden of managing patient flow may increase for nurses.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor the number and frequency of escalation huddles triggered by wait-time thresholds. Assess if the huddles effectively address the issue of prolonged wait times.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the number of huddles triggered by wait-time thresholds decreases and wait times improve, the option can be considered successful. However, if the number of huddles increases or wait times remain prolonged, further investigation may be needed.

options.title: Monitored bed management
options.description: Implement a system to protect reserve monitored beds for acute arrivals, especially during periods of high bed occupancy. Ensure that CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients have immediate access to these beds.
options.local_fit: This option is aligned with policy expectations and could improve patient access to monitored beds. However, it may require additional resources and coordination to ensure the availability of reserve beds.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to nurses and front desk staff if the system for managing monitored beds is not effectively communicated and implemented. Additionally, there may be a need for increased communication and coordination between different teams.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor the availability of monitored beds for CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients. Track the number of times these patients are placed in monitored beds promptly.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the availability of monitored beds for CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients improves consistently, the option can be considered successful. However, if the issue persists or worsens, further investigation into the root causes may be necessary.

options.title: Match rooming pace to clinician capacity
options.description: Investigate and understand the factors influencing physician pace during periods of high bed occupancy. Explore strategies to match the rooming pace with the capacity of clinicians, potentially reducing wait times.
options.local_fit: This option requires further investigation and may take time to implement. However, it aims to address the root cause of the issue, which is the slow physician pace.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to nurses and patients if the rooming pace is adjusted without considering the capacity of clinicians. Additionally, there may be a need for increased coordination between different teams to ensure a smooth flow of patients.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor the rooming pace during periods of high bed occupancy and compare it to the capacity of clinicians. Assess if adjusting the rooming pace improves wait times and patient flow.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the rooming pace can be effectively matched to clinician capacity, and wait times improve, the option can be considered successful. However, if the issue persists or worsens, further investigation into alternative strategies may be necessary.

recommendation.rationale: While all options have limited evidence strength, option O1 aligns with existing practices and can be implemented quickly. It aims to address the issue of prolonged wait times by triggering escalation huddles, which may help manage patient flow and reduce pressure on nurses and patients.
recommendation.would_change_if: If further evidence suggests that the root cause of the issue is not the slow physician pace, or if the implementation of option O1 does not lead to the desired improvements, the recommendation may change to focus on other options.

suggested_reviewers.why: To provide insights into the factors influencing physician pace and to ensure the effectiveness of the recommended option in managing patient flow.
To understand the impact of the recommended option on their workload and patient care, and to provide feedback on any potential pressure shifts.
